canonical_statement: Nephrotic-range proteinuria is defined as a spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of at least 200 mg/mmol (2 g/g), proteinuria of at least 1000 mg/m2 per day in a 24-hour sample, or the corresponding 3+ to 4+ urine dipstick range.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Nephrotic syndrome is defined as nephrotic-range proteinuria plus either hypoalbuminemia with serum albumin below 30 g/L (3 g/dL) or edema when the albumin level is unavailable.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Complete remission requires first-morning or 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at or below 200 mg/g (0.2 g/g or 20 mg/mmol), a negative or trace dipstick, or protein excretion below 100 mg/m2 per day on at least 3 consecutive days.

provenance.extractor_identifier: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol / ATOM SEA Literature Pipeline

canonical_statement: Partial remission is defined as first-morning or 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio above 200 mg/g but below 2 g/g, and, if available, serum albumin at least 30 g/L.

canonical_statement: Steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome is defined by complete remission within 4 weeks of standard-dose prednisone or prednisolone; steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome is defined by lack of complete remission within 4 weeks of daily standard-dose prednisone or prednisolone.

canonical_statement: Calcineurin inhibitor-responsive steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome is defined by partial remission within 6 months and/or complete remission within 12 months of adequate calcineurin inhibitor treatment; calcineurin inhibitor resistance is absence of partial remission after at least 6 months of adequate therapy.
